content:
Laredo Police Chief Miguel Rodriguez has confirmed that the man detained in the fatal early-morning stabbing on Texana Street is a U.S. Border Patrol agent, according to the Laredo Morning Times.

This is an update to Webb Watch's earlier story on the case, which police are calling Laredo's sixth homicide of 2026. Laredo police responded to multiple calls about a domestic disturbance in the 5500 block of Texana Street at about 2:45 a.m. on Wednesday, October 28, the Times reported.

A police drone pilot saw a vehicle leaving the area, and officers intercepted it, according to the Times. A 28-year-old woman was found alive in the rear floorboard of the vehicle with multiple stab wounds. She was taken to a hospital and later died.

The detained man is 30 years old, and no names had been released at the time of the Times report. Police said the case was being investigated as domestic violence, but the circumstances were still unclear Wednesday morning. Officers were awaiting a search warrant to process the scene and were seeking additional warrants for blood, saliva and other evidence, according to the report. Children reported inside the home were found unharmed after an emergency sweep.

The detained man is presumed innocent unless proven guilty in a court of law, and formal charges had not been announced in the earlier Webb Watch report. Webb Watch will update this story when police release names or a charging decision.

Sources:

  • Laredo Morning Times, “Border Patrol agent identified as suspect in fatal Laredo stabbing of a woman,” October 28, 2026
